title: Analytical vertical force-time measurement illustration
population: Equation-generated analytical signal; not athlete data.
metric: Vertical force over concentric time; shaded gross force and signed force-minus-bodyweight areas illustrate separate measurement definitions.
units: Force N; mass kg; time s; gross mean force N/kg; net impulse m/s.
grouping: One piecewise analytical curve with onset, peak, and takeoff boundaries.
sample_sizes: 361 evenly spaced time points for display; no empirical sample.
caption_tex: Analytical vertical force-time illustration, not observed athlete data. The displayed signal is generated with \(m=\SI{70}{\kilogram}\), \(g=\SI{9.80665}{\meter\per\second\squared}\), \(A=\SI{1000}{\newton}\), peak time \(t_p=\SI{0.22}{\second}\), and \(T=\SI{0.55}{\second}\). For \(0\leq t\leq t_p\), \(F_z(t)=mg+A\sin(\pi t/(2t_p))\); for \(t_p<t\leq T\), \(F_z(t)=(mg+A)[1-(t-t_p)/(T-t_p)]\). Concentric onset is \(t=0\), and takeoff is \(t=T\). The area under \(F_z\) defines gross mean force after division by \(mT\); the signed area between \(F_z\) and \(mg\) defines net impulse after division by \(m\). Units are N, kg, s, N/kg, and m/s as labeled.
